question.text:
The domain of definition of $f(x)=\sqrt{\frac{1-|x|}{2-|x|}}$ is Here $(a, b)=\{x: a    < x < b\}$ and
$[a, b]=\{x: a \leq x \leq b\}$

solution.text:
We have, $f(x)=\sqrt{\frac{1-|x|}{2-|x|}}$
$f(x)$ is defined for all $x$ satisfying $\frac{1-|x|}{2-|x|} \geq 0 \Rightarrow \frac{|x|-1}{|x|-2} \geq 0$
$\Rightarrow \quad|x| \leq$ lor $|x|>2$
$\Rightarrow \quad x \in[-1,1]$ or $x \in(-\infty,-2) \cup(2, \infty)$
$\Rightarrow \quad x \in(-\infty,-2) \cup[-1,1] \cup(2, \infty)$
